body:
Founder pushed back hard on my earlier 'couldn't reproduce it' answer, correctly -- a completely fresh Colab session with a freshly-pulled script still failed with the exact same TimeoutError at env.reset(). Found the real root cause this time by reproducing with the ACTUAL game mode the training script uses (MODE_QUEUE, not MODE_DEATHMATCH -- my earlier manual reproduction tests all used the wrong mode, a real mistake on my part) and by measuring log volume directly instead of guessing. Real bug: apps/server/src/main.c's per-tick [STATUS] print throttled by TICK COUNT (tick % 600 == 0) -- a reasonable ~10-second cadence at a normal server's own real ~60 ticks/sec, but --fast-forward decouples tick count from wall-clock time entirely (confirmed live: ~500K ticks/sec), so the identical modulo condition instead fires hundreds of times per second, unconditionally, even with zero clients connected. Measured directly: ~37KB/sec of log output in a verbose build. This print's own output used to go to subprocess.DEVNULL (discarded instantly, no cost) until my own earlier same-day fix (commit 4cff907) started capturing the training server's stdout to a real file for crash-diagnosis purposes -- a real, separately-justified fix that, combined with this pre-existing --fast-forward log-volume bug, is the most likely explanation for the founder's actual reported hang: writing that firehose continuously to a real file, worse on a slower/network-backed --output-dir (e.g. a Colab Drive mount), for an entire multi-hour training run is a real, serious I/O cost that can plausibly stall the server's own tick loop badly enough to miss a client's respawn window. Fixed at the source: the STATUS print now throttles by real wall-clock time (net_should_log_every, the exact same mechanism net_server_emit_summary right above it already uses) instead of tick count -- once per real second while a client is connected, once per real 10 seconds otherwise, regardless of tick rate. Live-verified BOTH correctness and volume with real, timed measurements: a real MODE_QUEUE client against the real live TRAINING_GROUND level under --fast-forward still connects and stays alive/welcomed exactly as before (unchanged behavior); log volume with zero clients dropped from 13627 lines/664KB over ~18s to 5 lines/234 bytes over 10s; with one connected client over ~20s, 36 lines/2004 bytes total, matching the intended real 1-second cadence exactly (confirmed via last_heard_ms deltas in the log itself) -- roughly a 350x reduction. make server/make lobby both clean. Commits: 9b2eee4 (fix) + b723b35 (changelog). Honest: I cannot 100% prove this was THE exact cause of the founder's specific Colab failure without their own crash-time server log, but it is a real, measured, previously-undiscovered bug that directly explains the reported symptom and coincides exactly with when the founder said things started failing (right after my own prior same-day logging change).

⚓ ☃
title: RL training: fixed real --fast-forward log flood that likely caused the reported hang
